title: Constructibility and evaluation for the scalar-perfect dual
statement: Let l be prime, k a field of positive characteristic p different from l, X separated of finite type over k and Λ an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring [sk-def-localizing-closure]. If P is locally constant perfect with scalar models [def-sfb-locally-constant-perfect-complex], then its specified relative dual P∨=RHom(P,Λ_X[0]) is bounded constructible in the finite constant model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For every object N of the full ambient unbounded derived module category there is an isomorphism RHom(P,N) ≅ P∨ tensor^L N for the existing relative tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. No boundedness or constructibility of N is required.

source.place: Step 6; perfect dual and tensor--Hom evaluation in paragraph 2

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality], $P^\vee$ is perfect and $\cHom_S(P,N)\simeq P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ for every ambient $N$. The slice-restriction assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies its restrictions with the duals of the local models. The scalar-cohomology formulas of [lem-sfb-internal-hom-dual-constructible-models] apply to the locally constant perfect models in the statement and put both $P$ and $P^\vee$ in $\Dbc(S,\Lambda)$, including completed integral coefficients. Finite Tor amplitude is established separately in Step 7. Specialize the normalized ringed-site duality through the exact internal-module comparison, and carry scalar presentations and cohomology through that equivalence. For the finite-subextension algebraic-closure ring use finite matrix descent to a finite coefficient subextension, rather than identifying it with the ring of all continuous algebraic-closure-valued functions.

source.place: Paragraph 2, perfect dual and tensor-Hom formula; paragraph 3, membership of the perfect factors.

proof.text:
Compare internal module objects with modules on the ringed site, preserving the
relative derived tensor, unit, internal Hom and slice restrictions. Pull the given
bounded finite-projective scalar complexes to the local charts. Finite projective
splittings give finite free retracts, so their duals are finite projective and the
canonical tensor--Hom evaluation is an isomorphism, also against an unbounded complex:
in every degree only finitely many source terms occur. Perfect duality and exact
slice restriction descend this canonical evaluation to the whole scheme. Scalar
cohomology models give bounded constructibility for the dual, including the completed
integral models and finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure. A finite affine
refinement of the cover exists since X is Noetherian and quasi-compact. The finitely
many bounded models have common cohomological bounds; descend their vanishing and
finite constant cohomology presentations by the cover criterion.
For empty X the cohomology is zero and has the empty stratification; evaluation is
then the unique isomorphism of zero objects. Finite Tor amplitude is a separate
assertion supplied by the existing dual Tor-amplitude theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem locallyConstantPerfect_dual_constructible
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hΛ : IsLocalizingAdmissibleCoefficient ℓ Λ)
    (P : (DerivedCategory
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))))
    (hP : IsLocallyConstantPerfectComplex Λ X P) :
    constantModelBoundedConstructible Λ X (relativeInternalHomDual (Mon.mk Λ) X P) ∧
    ∀ N : (DerivedCategory
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))),
      Nonempty (((derivedHom Λ X).obj (op P)).obj N ≅
      ((derivedTensor Λ X).obj (relativeInternalHomDual (Mon.mk Λ) X P)).obj N)
